name: Pythia staking-share transfers duplicate historical rewards
summary: PythiaTokenStaking adjusts reward points on mint and burn but inherits ERC20 transfers without adjustPointsForTransfer. Fresh recipients therefore claim historical rewards again; 140 helpers recycle the stake across six transactions.

loss.notes: Gross unauthorized reward quantity includes immediate payouts and helper-owned escrow entitlements. The conservative net USD floor values realized ETH less all initial ETH financing; full unmonetized-rights valuation remains unresolved (source-20).

limitations: Full episode USD valuation is unresolved; only an evidenced minimum is published.

Identity/age review: source-4 creates the direct staking ERC20 at block 20664393 index 80, timestamp 1725298319; source-1 executes it directly. eth_getCode at deployment, 20667433, 20667465 and 20667578 hashes to 0xcc40c98fa55f6ed38d88ccf79a12a3d1357aeef127b25fa0db61bb88a8b34b71. Verified source-5 has no upgrade, delegatecall or selfdestruct path. Constructor installs escrowPortion=0.5e18. Complete Etherscan V2 txlist(staking, 20664393–latest, ascending, offset 10000) returns 345 rows through block 22938702; pre-exploit setters configure deposit/reward PYT, fee receiver and 5% unstake fee. They select assets/exposure, not the missing transfer reward correction; no subsequent pre-exploit code or causal-state change. eth_getLogs(staking, 20664393–20669000) returns 1,460 logs: first non-mint/non-burn share transfer is source-1, and its trace confirms the first recycled-stake claim. Six payout transactions (source-1, sources 9–13) create 140 helper accounts. Only two subsequent share-transfer transactions have no payout. Source-8 replaces the distributor with 0xdead at block 20668032, making distributeRewards fail after the epoch; no later distributor reactivation in complete normal history. Escrow correctly consumes the inflated claim calculated by the staking artifact; it is custody evidence, not a separate defect-bearing target. Repository verifier reproduced all 12 declared anchor checks: PASS_ANCHORS on 2026-10-05 using configured Ethereum archive RPC.

Anchor/root-cause/loss review: source-5 mint/burn adjust pointsCorrection, but inherited transfer does not call AbstractRewards.adjustPointsForTransfer; source-1 claimRewards pays a fresh helper historical shareBasedPoints. Sum PYT Transfer logs from staking in source-1 and sources 9–13: 25,868.653168216188376592 to helpers plus 25,868.653168216188376529 to escrow, total 51,737.306336432376753121 PYT (18 decimals). Source-6 creates helper-owned vesting locks for the escrow half. Source-7 buys initial stake for 0.5 ETH; campaign restakes helper payouts. Final unstake source-14 returns 23,006.532525166631890329 PYT after the 5% fee. Sources 15–17 dispose of 23,006 PYT for respectively 11625077520775547675; 7381817829692341155; 1224729624735396938 wei WETH (sum 20,231,624,975,203,285,768), subsequently unwrapped. The minimum loss deducts the full 0.5 ETH initial financing from those proceeds, without deducting gas or fees again: 19.731624975203285768 ETH × source-18 price $2,514.03 (historical timestamp 1725336719). It omits unsold 0.532525166631890329 PYT and the 140 escrow entitlements; quantities are established but their USD value is unresolved. Next: inspect helper redemption permissions and escrow lock withdrawal/rescue history, then value or establish a lower bound for all unmonetized PYT rights. No full-episode USD amount is asserted.

limitations: Full episode USD value is unresolved: vested PYT rights and residual PYT are unvalued; loss carries a conservative net minimum.
